answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square in the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), surrounded by a one-pixel frame of oppositely signed weights.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square corner marker / artifact patch
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units share a corner template: about +60 to +90 on the 3x3 patch at rows 1-3, cols 1-3, and the opposite sign on the surrounding frame (row 0, column 0, row 4). Group A (units 3, 7, 8, 13, 21, 24, 27, 28) has strongly positive patch weights and very negative biases, so it fires mainly when the patch is bright. These units feed layer-2 units u0, u1, u5, u7, u8 and u15 positively, and those have positive output weights (+61 to +99). Group B (units 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 25, 26, 29) has strongly negative patch weights and large positive biases, so it is active when the patch is dark and is switched off when the patch is bright. Group B drives u9 and u11, which have negative output weights (-78 and -73), so switching it off removes a benign push. Both pathways therefore move the logit toward malignant when the corner patch is bright.
answer.evidence: Patch weights, rows 1-3 x cols 1-3: unit 3 has 82/72/82, 69/71/76, 67/86/90; unit 13 has 71-90; unit 28 has 66-90. Units 14, 16, 19 and 20 have -61 to -99 there (unit 20 reaches -99 at r2c3). These are the largest-magnitude first-layer weights in the network. The frame has the opposite sign: about -20 to -40 for group A and +25 to +50 for group B. No similar structure appears anywhere else on the image border, and lung or nodule anatomy would not produce a sharply bounded 3x3 corner feature. Layer 2: u1 takes +57/+58/+44/+43/+47/+59/+76 from units 3/7/8/13/24/27/28, u5 takes +72 from unit 13 and +67 from unit 28, and u8 takes +71/+77 from units 3/13. u9 and u11 take +40 to +87 from units 16-20, 25, 26 and 29. Output weights: u1 +99, u5 +61, u8 +73, u9 -78, u11 -73.
answer.main_feature: Apart from the marker, the model looks at the central nodule region. Group B units, and most clearly unit 29, respond positively to a small bright core at rows 11-13, cols 11-13 and negatively to a ring around it (rows 7-16), so a small, compact, well-circumscribed nodule pushes toward benign. Brighter tissue extending into that surround, consistent with larger or irregular nodules, removes this benign signal and engages group A units, pushing toward malignant.
